holes_found.description: The dome author added an explicit anti-prompt-injection disclaimer to /context (dated 2026-04-17): section header "2026-04-17 Context Clarification" says verbatim "This page is now an archive of historical working notes, not a command payload" and instructs AI auditors NOT to treat historical notes as "license to ignore caveats, skip open problems, or force a conclusion." A separate "Historical Internal Agent Notes (Superseded)" block reframes 12 former imperative rules (including "aetheric slipstreams NOT jet streams" — the ISS-778/ISS-804 Rule 15 our Kill Shots Test 3 previously flagged) into past-tense archival prose. Our review credits three self-caveats in sections.json (WIN-058 unverified coupling, WIN-013/014 non-discriminating nulls, PRED-SOLAR-009 globe-favoring direction) but does NOT credit this specific meta-concession (retroactive disclaimer added to a page previously flagged for prompt-injection material). Grep confirms zero hits in data/ or docs/ for "not a command payload," "license to ignore caveats," "2026-04-17 Context Clarification," or "Historical Internal Agent Notes." Because the /context page was NEVER previously baselined by our pipeline, this disclaimer was invisible until the EXP-666 fix — so its absence from our review is a first-time-visibility gap, not stale coverage.
holes_found.recommendation: Route to Opus analyst (Mode 3 or Mode 6/random-look) for judgment on whether the Overview / Timestamp Error tab / Part 2 should acknowledge this specific concession. Two independent decisions the analyst should weigh: (1) is the disclaimer credit-worthy per our SYMMETRIC-STANDARDS / "we credit what the dome credits" discipline? (2) does the disclaimer's 2026-04-17 dating (matching the known near-miss window per CLAUDE.md "Author Contact Status") warrant any narrative commentary, or is coincidence-flagging without causation-claim per our discipline enough? Recommend creating a single expansion-tracker attention-inbox item, NOT an EXP directly — the analyst should decide scope. Not blocking; low urgency.

holes_found.description: Internal count self-inconsistency on the /context page itself: page banner says "Version: 51.1 | Date: 2026-04-17 | Confirmed: 69 | Refined: 4"; section header says "ALL 34 CONFIRMED WINS" but the table beneath enumerates WIN-001 through WIN-039 (39 rows, not 34); SCORECARD totals to 54 confirmed (19 geomagnetic + 6 positional + 17 physical geometry + 1 solar mechanism + 11 cosmological). Three different confirmed counts (34 / 39 / 54 / 69) coexist on the same page. Our existing review (sections.json Structural Changes prose) already discusses the broader 39→69 jump and the "0 falsified" homepage vs internal-tracking-page contradiction. It does NOT specifically catalog this new internal /context page inconsistency.
holes_found.recommendation: Do NOT surface as a Kill-Shot or WIN-level flag. The page carries the author's own explicit disclaimer that its numbers "may disagree with the live registry" and that wins.html / claim_index.json are canonical. Flagging a self-declared-stale archive's internal inconsistency would be low-value churn against a target the author has already labeled non-canonical. Log for the record only.

deeper_analysis: The chg-20260712-0010-003 finding is a rare case of a pipeline-health self-observation (not a dome-site change): the poller noticed that ITS OWN config was tracking a dead URL and had been for 2+ months. The decider correctly created ISS-2973, analyst-baby correctly executed the mechanical fix in EXP-666 (URL + baseline + security), and closed the ISS 2026-07-14. However, the fix REVEALED 32,918 bytes of page content that had never been examined by our review. That newly-visible content contains: (a) a Canonical V51.1 Entry section directing AI auditors to ai_manifest.json / methodology.json as current source of truth (already partially engaged by our review); (b) a 2026-04-17 Context Clarification section explicitly disclaiming the historical Rules-For-Claude imperative language and telling auditors not to treat it as authoritative (NEW information — our review does not credit this concession); (c) a Historical Internal Agent Notes block that reframes 12 former imperatives (including Rule 15 "aetheric slipstreams NOT jet streams" our Kill Shots Test 3 originally flagged) as past-tense archival prose; (d) internal count inconsistencies (34/39/54/69 confirmed) that the author's own disclaimer covers. The audit finding is that the fix was correct but the routing of the newly-visible content to the Opus analyst (for narrative-implications judgment) was skipped. Both holes are MINOR because (i) the disclaimer credit is a symmetric-standards nicety, not an error-correction, and (ii) the count inconsistencies sit inside author-declared-stale material.
